paragraphs: AD-PT investigates how to pretrain a point-cloud perception model so that its learned representations transfer across autonomous-driving datasets and models. The paper identifies a restriction in earlier work: pretraining and fine-tuning commonly happen on the same benchmark. That arrangement makes it difficult to establish whether a pretrained model provides broadly reusable knowledge.

The authors build a large pretraining dataset with diverse point-cloud distributions and treat learning as a semi-supervised problem. A small amount of labeled data accompanies a much larger unlabeled collection. During backbone training, the approach increases diversity at both the scene and individual-object levels and develops the model's ability to learn from unfamiliar instances.

The resulting backbone representations can support multiple downstream models and benchmarks, separating pretraining from a particular fine-tuning task. The authors report significant perception improvements on Waymo, nuScenes, and KITTI using models including PV-RCNN++, SECOND, and CenterPoint. These results support the usefulness of diverse pretraining for transfer across the evaluated settings, making reusable perception backbones the central contribution.
neurips-2023-ad-pt-autonomous-driving-pr.tldr: AD-PT uses diverse, largely unlabeled point clouds to pretrain reusable perception backbones that improve multiple autonomous-driving benchmarks.

paragraphs: GRACE addresses the problem of repeatedly correcting a deployed language model as its inputs, user requirements, and knowledge needs change. Retraining can be expensive, while existing editing methods can lose performance after many successive corrections. The aim is therefore to accumulate targeted repairs while keeping unrelated behavior largely intact.

The method stores new mappings inside the model's latent representation space without changing its original weights. These mappings form a discrete, local codebook of edits: corrections are represented as localized additions to the model's behavior. GRACE builds this codebook from errors arriving over time, allowing the editing process to continue as new problems are discovered.

The authors report thousands of sequential edits using only this stream of errors. Experiments with T5, BERT, and GPT models show state-of-the-art performance at applying and retaining corrections, together with generalization to unseen inputs. The findings matter because successful continual editing requires both remembering earlier fixes and extending them beyond the exact examples that prompted them.
neurips-2023-aging-with-grace-lifelong-m.tldr: GRACE stores localized corrections in a model's latent space, enabling thousands of sequential edits without changing its pretrained weights.

paragraphs: This paper studies the computational cost of determining which neurons activate during neural-network training. For n data points, m neurons, and d input features, evaluating an entire layer conventionally takes time proportional to nmd per iteration. Earlier work reduced the iteration cost below that order, but required exponential preprocessing of the data or weights.

The proposed method stores correlations between weights and data in a tree structure. This structure supports quickly detecting active neurons as training changes the weights. Its preprocessing takes O(nmd) time, while each subsequent iteration still takes o(nmd) time. The contribution therefore removes the exponential setup cost while retaining the stated asymptotic improvement in repeated training work.

The authors also establish a conditional lower bound for dynamically identifying firing neurons. Assuming a conjecture from complexity theory, their algorithm cannot be substantially accelerated for that task. This result places the speedup in a theoretical context: the method improves preprocessing costs, and its dynamic detection component is close to a computational barrier under the conjecture.
neurips-2023-bypass-exponential-time-pre.tldr: A tree of weight–data correlations reduces neuron-detection costs during training without the exponential preprocessing required by earlier work.

paragraphs: This paper develops neural-network control policies together with formal guarantees about their behavior in stochastic environments. Its goal is to certify that a behavioral specification holds with a desired probability. The approach uses the compositional structure of specifications written in SpectRL, breaking a complex requirement into a graph of smaller control tasks.

Each task is a probabilistic reach-avoid problem: the policy must reach a target while avoiding specified outcomes. The method learns an individual policy alongside a reach-avoid supermartingale, a mathematical certificate supporting a probability guarantee for that task. It then combines these policies and certificates to obtain a global policy satisfying the overall specification.

The authors also derive a tighter lower bound on the reach-avoid success probability certified by a supermartingale. This matters when multiple component policies must be combined, because their guarantees need to support an acceptable probability for the complete task. A prototype is evaluated in the Stochastic Nine Rooms environment, demonstrating the proposed learning-and-certification framework in that setting.
neurips-2023-compositional-policy-learni.tldr: The method composes neural control policies and mathematical certificates to guarantee specified behavior with a desired probability.

paragraphs: Credal networks describe probabilistic relationships while allowing uncertainty about the probability values themselves. This paper studies marginal MAP inference in those networks: finding the most likely assignment to a selected group of variables while accounting for the remaining variables. The task combines choosing an assignment with evaluating probabilities under imprecisely specified distributions.

The difficulty extends beyond searching through candidate assignments. Evaluating even a complete candidate requires exact likelihood calculations involving combinatorial sums over vertices of a complex joint credal set. That set represents the possible marginal distributions of the selected variables, so uncertainty about probabilities creates additional computational work within the search.

The authors develop exact algorithms using variable elimination and depth-first search, alongside approximation methods using mini-bucket partitioning and stochastic local search. This supplies multiple approaches to the same difficult inference problem, including methods that pursue exact answers and methods that approximate them. Extensive experiments on random instances and real-world benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods across the evaluated problems.
neurips-2023-credal-marginal-map-6dc443f.tldr: The paper develops exact and approximate algorithms for finding likely variable assignments in networks with imprecise probabilities.

paragraphs: Statistical downscaling converts coarse simulation outputs into plausible detailed outputs consistent with a higher-fidelity simulator. This paper addresses a setting where the coarse simulator is biased and matching low- and high-resolution training examples are unavailable. The objective is a conditional distribution of detailed outcomes, allowing more than one plausible refinement of an input.

The framework separates correction from refinement. An optimal transport map first debiases the coarse data. A probabilistic diffusion model then upsamples it using conditional sampling applied afterward. Combining these transformations lets the method learn from unpaired data while addressing both systematic discrepancies in the input and the need to generate finer detail.

Experiments on one- and two-dimensional fluid flows produce realistic outputs at 8× and 16× higher resolutions and recover relevant physical statistics. The procedure also matches these statistics when input and output low-frequency content differ. This matters because the alternatives discussed in the abstract depend on matching that coarse-scale content, an assumption that biased simulations can make difficult to satisfy.
neurips-2023-debias-coarsely-sample-cond.tldr: A two-stage method debiases coarse simulations and uses diffusion to generate statistically faithful high-resolution outputs from unpaired data.

paragraphs: DiffPack predicts protein side-chain configurations when the protein backbone is given. The paper emphasizes that this geometry has strong constraints: covalent bond lengths and bond angles are fixed, leaving torsional angles as the adjustable quantities. Learning directly in that space addresses restrictions that existing regression-based machine-learning approaches overlook.

The model learns a joint distribution over side-chain torsional angles through a diffusion process that adds and removes noise in torsional space. Rather than perturbing all four angles simultaneously, it generates them sequentially, from χ1 through χ4. Separate diffusion models for the angles support this autoregressive construction and avoid the issues associated with changing every angle at once.

On side-chain packing benchmarks, the authors report angle-accuracy improvements of 11.9% on CASP13 and 13.5% on CASP14, together with a model using 60 times fewer parameters. They also demonstrate improvements to AlphaFold2 side-chain predictions. These findings support representing the prediction problem through its geometric degrees of freedom and generating their dependencies sequentially.
neurips-2023-diffpack-a-torsional-diffus.tldr: DiffPack generates protein side-chain torsional angles sequentially with diffusion, improving benchmark accuracy with substantially fewer model parameters.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a data structure for sampling rows from a Khatri-Rao product according to its exact leverage-score distribution. The product combines several matrices and can have an enormous number of rows. Sampling from it efficiently matters because the resulting samples can form smaller versions of linear least-squares problems used in tensor decomposition.

Each sampled row requires time logarithmic in the product's row count and quadratic in its column count. The persistent storage overhead is no larger than the input matrices themselves. These properties make sampling tractable even when each matrix contributing to the product contains tens of millions of rows.

The authors apply the sampler to sketch least-squares problems in Candecomp/PARAFAC decomposition and obtain a lower asymptotic cost per solve than recent competing methods. Experiments on billion-scale sparse tensors and synthetic data support the theoretical analysis, with higher accuracy than competitors as decomposition rank increases. Exactness here concerns the sampling distribution; the sampled least-squares problems are still sketches of the original problems.
neurips-2023-fast-exact-leverage-score-s.tldr: An efficient exact leverage-score sampler makes large Khatri-Rao products usable for faster, accurate tensor-decomposition sketches.

paragraphs: This paper considers imitation learning when people cannot reliably rank demonstrations of similar quality. Its feedback setting assumes that an annotator can correctly distinguish a pair when one demonstration is expert and the other is non-expert. This captures a weaker form of supervision than requiring a clear preference for every pair.

The authors model the demonstration collection as a mixture of expert and non-expert data. Under this formulation, they show that the expert policy distribution can be recovered when the proportion of expert examples, α, is known. When that proportion is unknown, they propose a method to estimate it before using the recovered distribution.

The recovered expert distribution is incorporated into generative adversarial imitation learning to create an end-to-end algorithm. Experiments across several tasks show better performance than standard and preference-based imitation methods. The contribution is a way to extract useful expert behavior from ambiguous comparisons, with the recovery result tied to the mixture formulation and knowledge of the expert proportion.
neurips-2023-imitation-learning-from-vag.tldr: A mixture-based approach learns expert behavior from feedback that reliably distinguishes only clearly different demonstration qualities.

paragraphs: Mechanic automates the choice of a learning-rate scale factor for an existing optimization algorithm and schedule. This factor controls the overall scale of the learning rate used during training. The paper targets a practical tuning decision that otherwise requires manual selection, while allowing the base optimizer and its schedule to remain part of the training setup.

The method turns recent theoretical reductions from online convex optimization into a practical tuning technique. Its stated scope covers any base optimization algorithm and schedule. The core contribution is therefore an automatic mechanism for setting their learning-rate scale, connecting a theoretical approach to the demands of large-scale deep-learning training.

The authors evaluate Mechanic across large-scale tasks with different batch sizes, schedules, and optimization algorithms. Depending on the problem, it comes close to manually tuned learning rates, matches them, or improves on them. This variation is central to interpreting the findings: the experiments support competitive automatic tuning across the tested settings, without claiming that it always exceeds manual tuning.
neurips-2023-mechanic-a-learning-rate-tu.tldr: Mechanic automatically tunes learning-rate scale and approaches, matches, or improves on manual tuning across evaluated deep-learning tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to identify the best action for several related bilinear bandit tasks using fewer observations. Each action selects a pair of arms from two entity types, and its reward depends bilinearly on their known feature vectors. The pure-exploration objective is to discover the best pair for each task.

The tasks are assumed to share a low-dimensional linear representation. The proposed GOBLIN algorithm uses experimental design to decide how to allocate samples, addressing two connected needs: learning the common representation and identifying optimal pairs within individual tasks. Observations therefore contribute both to shared understanding and to resolving each task's own choices.

The authors provide a sample-complexity analysis for this shared-representation setting, describing how many samples the identification process requires. Their results show significant improvements over solving the tasks independently. The benefit rests on the shared structure: learning a useful representation across tasks reduces the amount of separate exploration needed to find their respective best actions.
neurips-2023-multi-task-representation-l.tldr: GOBLIN exploits a shared low-dimensional representation to identify optimal arm pairs across bilinear bandit tasks with fewer samples.

paragraphs: This paper studies allocating resources fairly over time against an unrestricted adversary. Performance is compared with the best fixed allocation chosen with knowledge of the entire sequence. The objective uses aggregate α-fair utilities, whose global, non-separable structure makes decisions difficult to evaluate independently. Earlier results rule out sublinear standard regret for this problem.

The proposed Online Fair Allocation policy instead achieves sublinear approximate regret. For 0 ≤ α < 1, its approximation factor is (1−α) raised to the power −(1−α), which is at most 1.445. The guarantee relaxes the comparison with the hindsight benchmark, allowing the regret to grow more slowly than time despite the impossibility for standard regret.

The upper bound exhibits a phase transition at α = 1/2, changing from power-law growth to a constant. The result also resolves an online job-scheduling question in certain parameter regimes. Supporting techniques include estimating future gradients for non-additive rewards and bootstrapping second-order regret bounds, providing tools for reasoning about these globally coupled objectives.
neurips-2023-no-regret-algorithms-for-fa.tldr: Online Fair Allocation achieves sublinear approximate regret for adversarial fair allocation, with a bound that changes regime at α = 1/2.

paragraphs: Noether Embedding learns representations of temporal regularities in events, aiming to form them from limited examples and retrieve them efficiently. The paper argues that existing event embeddings struggle to determine whether such regularities hold, even after their vectors have been trained. It treats learning a pattern and later querying it as connected representation problems.

The method builds time-translation symmetry into the embedding space through conserved local energies. This structural constraint reduces checking a regularity's validity to embedding individual event samples. The authors describe the resulting formation process as data-efficient and insensitive to sample size, and report constant-time complexity for retrieving temporal regularities.

Evaluation separates detection of valid regularities from queries about their intervals, using ICEWS14, ICEWS18, and GDELT. Noether Embedding achieves roughly twice the detection F1 scores of classic embeddings and more than ten times their interval-query confidence scores. These are distinct reported measures, supporting both detection and retrieval capabilities. The authors also illustrate potential uses in social-event prediction, personal decisions, and memory-constrained settings.
neurips-2023-noether-embedding-efficient.tldr: Noether Embedding encodes time-translation symmetry to learn temporal regularities efficiently and retrieve them in constant time.

paragraphs: This paper examines how the definition of perceptual realism affects causal, low-latency video compression. It compares two perception losses alongside mean squared error. One evaluates the joint distribution of frames through the current frame; the other evaluates individual frame distributions. The difference determines whether realism explicitly includes relationships across time.

Information-theoretic analysis and experiments reveal a consequential tradeoff, especially at low bit rates. The joint-distribution loss can preserve temporal correlations better, but it brings a substantial distortion penalty and makes recovery from earlier reconstruction errors harder. Thus, enforcing realistic relationships between frames can affect both reconstruction accuracy and how mistakes persist through a sequence.

The authors also show that this choice can sometimes be deferred to decoding. Representations trained using only mean squared error can be near universal, supporting reconstructions close to optimal under either perception loss. Analysis of a Gauss-Markov source and experiments on moving MNIST and KTH support the results, suggesting scope to separate encoding from the decoder's chosen realism criterion.
neurips-2023-on-the-choice-of-perception.tldr: Video perception losses create different temporal-consistency and distortion tradeoffs, while some MSE-trained encodings can support either loss at decoding.

paragraphs: Independent component analysis seeks hidden sources that generate observed data. Traditional approaches often assume non-Gaussian sources because Gaussian distributions have rotational symmetries that make source recovery ambiguous. This paper develops an identifiability theory that accommodates Gaussian sources, asking when the hidden generative structure can be determined from second-order statistics.

The theory shifts the relevant restrictions toward the connections between sources and observed variables. It introduces a structural-variability assumption that the authors show is necessary and considerably less restrictive than connective assumptions in recent work. The result does not eliminate structural requirements; it offers a route to identifiability without imposing additional distributional preconditions on the sources.

The authors also propose two estimation methods that combine second-order statistics with a sparsity constraint. Experiments validate the theoretical account and the proposed estimators. The significance is that information about sparse source-to-observation connections can support recovery in settings where a non-Gaussianity assumption would exclude the source distributions of interest.
neurips-2023-on-the-identifiability-of-s.tldr: The paper establishes sparse ICA identifiability using structural assumptions and second-order statistics without requiring non-Gaussian sources.

paragraphs: A self-consistent field equation is an eigenvalue problem in which the matrix depends on its own eigenvectors. Solving it requires finding a mutually consistent matrix and set of vectors. Such equations matter in computational science through their connection to the Schrödinger equation, but traditional fixed-point iterations can fail to converge.

The paper reinterprets this circular dependence as principal component analysis on a changing time series. A distribution and its leading principal components update one another over time, with equilibrium corresponding to a solution of the original equation. This perspective makes online PCA techniques available as tools for guiding the coupled updates toward consistency.

Using this formulation and several numerical adaptations, the authors develop a new SCF solution algorithm. Experiments on synthetic problems and real electronic-structure scenarios demonstrate strong convergence capability. The contribution is both conceptual and algorithmic: it connects a nonlinear scientific-computing problem to an online learning formulation and uses that connection to improve convergence in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-online-pca-in-converging-se.tldr: Recasting self-consistent field equations as evolving PCA enables an algorithm with strong convergence results on synthetic and electronic-structure problems.

paragraphs: This paper studies games where agents' actions change population data, which then feeds back into the agents' strategic decisions. The objective is to learn a Nash equilibrium under bandit feedback. In this setting, the agents are strategically coupled and cannot simply rely on an oracle supplying the gradients needed by conventional gradient methods.

The authors represent strategic interactions with a general parametric model and approximate the unknown gradient through that model. Their Online Performative Gradient Descent algorithm combines online stochastic approximation with projected gradient descent. This provides a procedure for learning the information needed to update decisions while accounting for the decision-dependent nature of the game.

The efficiency guarantee applies to strongly monotone decision-dependent games under assumptions on the parametric model's function classes, described by the authors as mild. Within that setting, they prove that OPGD can efficiently find a Nash equilibrium. Synthetic numerical experiments support the analysis, connecting the gradient-approximation strategy to the stated equilibrium-learning guarantee.
neurips-2023-online-performative-gradien.tldr: OPGD learns Nash equilibria from bandit feedback using gradient approximation, with efficiency guarantees for strongly monotone games under stated modeling assumptions.

paragraphs: This paper examines why learning useful features can involve tradeoffs among data, network size, training time, and random initialization. It begins with offline sparse parity classification, where a statistical-query lower bound applies to gradient-based multilayer-perceptron training. The bound describes a resource frontier: successful learning requires enough capacity, examples, iterations, or favorable random guesses.

Theory and experiments show that sparse initialization and greater network width improve sample efficiency in this setting. Width acts as parallel search, increasing the chance that some neurons begin in favorable configurations for learning sparse features. This provides a mechanism connecting a larger network to reduced data requirements in the studied problem.

The authors then investigate sparse parity as a proxy for real tasks requiring axis-aligned feature learning. Wide, sparsely initialized multilayer perceptrons improve sample efficiency on tabular classification benchmarks and sometimes outperform tuned random forests. These results support the usefulness of the synthetic task for studying particular feature-learning demands, while preserving the qualified nature of the benchmark comparison.
neurips-2023-pareto-frontiers-in-deep-fe.tldr: Sparse-parity analysis explains how width and sparse initialization can trade model capacity for better sample efficiency in feature learning.

paragraphs: This paper studies learners whose predictions come with provable correctness guarantees when test conditions are challenging. It considers several forms of adversarial test-time attack as well as natural distribution shifts. The motivation is that earlier learning-theoretic guarantees address only specific settings, leaving a need for reliability analyses that cover these changing test environments.

The authors develop a reliable learner and prove that its guarantees are optimal in the settings they consider. They also discuss computationally feasible implementations. Together, these contributions address both the strength of the correctness guarantees and how the proposed learner could be implemented, rather than treating reliability solely as an abstract existence question.

Positive performance guarantees are established for several structured examples, including linear separators under log-concave distributions and classifiers with smooth boundaries under smooth probability distributions. These examples make the theory concrete by connecting the learner's guarantees to specified classifier and distribution families. The result expands the theoretical treatment of reliable prediction under adversarial changes and natural shifts within the analyzed settings.
neurips-2023-reliable-learning-in-challe.tldr: The paper develops a reliable learner with provably optimal guarantees for studied adversarial attacks and natural distribution shifts.

paragraphs: This paper addresses repairing neural networks trained on problematic data, such as corrupted inputs or noisy labels. Existing repair approaches identify harmful training examples and remove their influence. The authors point out that a flagged example may contain useful information as well as harmful information, and clean examples can also be flagged mistakenly.

Their method uses knowledge from a retained clean dataset to guide repair. It first identifies potentially harmful examples, then separates beneficial and detrimental information within them. The extracted beneficial information is used to improve the model. This makes the repair process sensitive to the information inside an example rather than treating identification as sufficient reason to erase its full contribution.

Empirical evaluations show improvements over baseline methods in both harmful-data identification and model repair. The advantage is especially clear when identification is difficult and many benign examples are implicated: the proposed method improves performance while baselines deteriorate after removing useful information. The findings support preserving valuable training signals during repair, with the retained clean set supplying the guiding knowledge.
neurips-2023-retaining-beneficial-inform.tldr: A clean-set-guided repair method separates useful and harmful information in flagged training data, improving repair while retaining beneficial signals.

paragraphs: TACO addresses the large amount of interaction data needed to learn control from images. The paper argues that auxiliary prediction tasks can fail to retain enough information for optimal policies or value functions. It also emphasizes action representations, which deserve particular attention when controls are continuous rather than a small set of discrete choices.

The method jointly learns latent representations of states and actions through temporal contrastive learning. Its objective increases mutual information between a current state paired with an action sequence and the corresponding future state. The authors provide a theoretical account showing that the learned representations can contain sufficient information for control, linking this learning objective to sample efficiency.

For online learning, TACO delivers an average 40% performance improvement after one million environment interactions across nine challenging visual continuous-control tasks from DeepMind Control Suite. It also works as an added module for existing offline visual reinforcement-learning methods, achieving reported state-of-the-art performance across datasets of varying quality. These findings support learning action and state representations together in both evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-texttt-taco-temporal-latent.tldr: TACO jointly learns state and action representations through temporal contrastive learning, improving online and offline visual control performance.

paragraphs: This paper adapts transformers to directed acyclic graphs, where directed relationships contain no cycles. The central challenge is making a transformer respect the graph's structure while retaining its ability to learn complex relationships. The authors focus on structural information specific to DAGs, including the partial order induced by their directed connections.

The architecture introduces two complementary changes. Its attention mechanism captures DAG structure while being substantially more efficient than ordinary quadratic transformer attention. A positional encoding represents the graph's partial order, supplying an additional way to express which elements precede others. Together, these changes make both attention and positional information reflect the type of graph being processed.

The authors evaluate the approach on tasks ranging from source-code graph classification to classifying nodes in citation networks. In these evaluations, the adaptations help graph transformers generally outperform graph neural networks designed for DAGs, and improve state-of-the-art graph transformers in quality and efficiency. The results support tailoring transformer structure to the ordering relationships already present in DAG data.
neurips-2023-transformers-over-directed-.tldr: DAG-specific attention and positional encodings improve graph-transformer quality and efficiency across evaluated graph and node classification tasks.

paragraphs: Compressing messages in distributed optimization reduces the data sent in each communication round, but the introduced distortion can require more rounds. This paper asks when compression actually lowers the total communication needed to reach a desired solution. It develops a theoretical formulation for studying that tradeoff with unbiased compressors.

The analysis shows that unbiasedness alone does not necessarily save total communication. Savings can be achieved when the compressors used by different workers are also independent. For smooth convex optimization, the authors establish lower bounds on the required communication rounds and show that a refined analysis of ADIANA matches them, making those bounds tight.

When local smoothness constants share a common upper bound, independent unbiased compression can reduce total communication by a factor up to order √min{n, κ}, with n workers and condition number κ. Experiments support the theory. The result identifies both a sufficient additional condition for savings and how the possible benefit scales with the number of workers and the optimization problem's conditioning.
neurips-2023-unbiased-compression-saves-.tldr: Independent unbiased compressors can reduce total distributed-optimization communication under stated conditions, whereas unbiasedness alone does not ensure savings.

paragraphs: This paper investigates why text-to-image diffusion models sometimes reproduce images from their training data. Such copying can occur without users realizing that an output closely replicates an existing example. The authors examine memorization with particular attention to the role of text conditioning, extending the discussion beyond repeated images in the training collection.

Their experiments indicate that text conditioning plays a role comparable in importance to image duplication. Replication often does not occur in the unconditional models they study, while it is common in the text-conditioned case. This is an empirical pattern rather than a claim that unconditional generation cannot copy or that every text-conditioned model will do so.

Motivated by these observations, the authors propose techniques for reducing replication during training and inference, centered on randomizing and augmenting captions. The approach makes the textual side of generation part of the mitigation strategy. Its significance is to identify caption information as a useful intervention point alongside concerns about duplicate training images, broadening how the copying problem can be addressed.
neurips-2023-understanding-and-mitigatin.tldr: Experiments identify text conditioning as an important contributor to diffusion-model copying and motivate caption-based mitigation techniques.

paragraphs: This paper estimates optical flow from spike-camera streams while addressing how much temporal data to use. Selecting an appropriate stream length is important for extracting precise information. The proposed dynamic timing representation captures several temporal scales, giving the model access to features describing different spans of the spike sequence.

A multilayer architecture uses dilated convolutions along time to obtain these features with few parameters. Layer attention then combines them dynamically. The authors pair this representation with an unsupervised, spike-based learning method for optical flow, removing dependence on labeled training data. They also construct SSES, a synthetic validation dataset containing extreme autonomous-driving scenarios and corner cases.

Experiments demonstrate optical-flow prediction in multiple high-speed settings, including real scenes. On PHM, the method reduces error relative to SCFlow by 15% at Δt = 10 and 19% at Δt = 20 under the same settings used in prior work. These results support combining adaptive temporal features with unsupervised learning for the evaluated spike-stream motion-estimation tasks.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-optical-flow-e.tldr: Dynamic temporal features and unsupervised learning improve spike-camera optical-flow estimation across evaluated high-speed scenes.
